1) The use of bioinformatics approaches to predict transcription-factor binding sites and regulatory elements is a powerful tool to understand the regulation of drug metabolizing enzymes.

the expression of drug-methabolizing enzymes can be predicted using the cis-regulatory elements of transcription factor binding sites and that these elements can be identified using bioinformatics methods.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational tools for the prediction of cis-regulatory motifs for transcription factors, which are known to be induced by drugs.
the prediction of cis-regulatory DNA elements for transcription factors involved in the regulation of the expression of drug metabolising enzymes and transporters.
the prediction of cis-regulatory sequences in the genome, and their subsequent analysis using bioinformatics methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of transcription factor prediction is still in a state of rapid flux and that the most reliable prediction method will probably be the one that uses a combination of the various methods.
the use of computational methods to identify regulatory elements is still in its infancy and that there is no single best way to predict regulatory elements.
the prediction of cis-regulatory interactions is a very complex task, but that it is a task well worth undertaking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of bioinformatics methods for the prediction of transcription factor binding sites can be a valuable tool to understand the regulatory networks of genes involved in drug disposition.
we have developed a method that can predict the cis-regulatory elements of a drug-activated transcription factor with high accuracy and specificity.
the prediction of cis-regulatory DNA sequences for drug-activated TFs is possible and that the prediction of regulatory networks is a feasible goal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to predict cis-regulatory elements with a reasonable degree of accuracy using a combination of sequence-based approaches and in vitro reporter assays.
it is possible to identify the transcription factor binding sites that are involved in the induction of the drug-metabolism genes.
it is possible to use existing data to make accurate predictions about the regulation of drug metabolising enzymes and transporters by transcription factors.
